review.tagline: Python tool that converts PDF, Office, HTML and audio files to Markdown for LLMs
review.summary: MarkItDown is a Python library and CLI that converts PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, images, audio, HTML, CSV/JSON/XML, ZIP, EPUB and YouTube URLs into Markdown, keeping headings, lists, tables and links. Optional backends add LLM image descriptions, Azure Document Intelligence, Azure Content Understanding, and OCR via the markitdown-ocr plugin. Output targets LLM pipelines rather than high-fidelity human-facing documents.
review.audience: Developers feeding documents into LLM and RAG pipelines
strengths: Covers many formats through one CLI and Python API (convert, convert_local, convert_stream)
Built-in converters run offline; install only needed formats via extras like [pdf,docx,pptx]
Third-party plugin system, plus an LLM-vision OCR plugin using any OpenAI-compatible client
MIT license, active releases, Python 3.10 through 3.14
weaknesses: Not meant for high-fidelity conversion; output is tuned for text analysis tools
Video and structured field extraction need billable Azure Content Understanding
convert() accepts URIs and files with process privileges; untrusted input must be sanitized
LLM image descriptions currently limited to pptx and image files; OCR needs a plugin
needs: Needs Python 3.10-3.14, Azure Document Intelligence (optional), Azure Content Understanding (optional), OpenAI-compatible client (optional)
